Cracking encryption via brute force (i.e. without the help of a vulnerability in the encryption method) is ludicrously difficult, mainly because the longer the password the longer the brute force attack needs to be, and it scales up exponentially. If your password is 5 characters or less long then it can be brute forced in less than an hour. If it's 10 or more long than it can't be brute forced within our lifespans with our current tech (meaning we'd die before it finished).

Here's a fun little tool to calculate how long brute force attacks take: http://lastbit.com/pswcalc.asp

When I used to encrypt things I would never use passwords with fewer than 30 characters.

Of course, if the government REALLY wanted your files, they may have the resources to find an encryption vulnerability.

Or install a keylogger. But that's unlikely as I am a upstanding citizen and a pillar of my community :)
